Follow MCDA_paper_results_spec.md. If anything here contradicts it, stop and ask before running.

GOAL
Build an alternative Malta street greenery indicator from the Meta and WRI 1 m canopy height map, compare it with the current one (perc_tree, Urban Atlas 2018 Street Tree Layer), and rerun the score and Step 3 with it. Do NOT overwrite any current score file, table or figure: everything new gets the suffix _canopy. Do not touch the HIA code (the HIA uses its own street tree fraction).

Work in a new notebook: mcda/street_greenery_canopy_malta.Rmd

STEP 0. Checks before anything else
a. Grid: Malta must have 10,657 cells. If not, stop and report.
b. Find where perc_tree is read and how it becomes a priority score (direction, normalisation, Table S1). Report: number of distinct values, share of scored cells at the most common value, share at maximum priority (expected about 90%).

STEP 1. Download the canopy height map
a. Source: s3://dataforgood-fb-data (public, no AWS account, anonymous access). Prefer version 2: first list forests/v2/global/ and find the tile index. If version 2 has no usable index, use version 1: forests/v1/alsgedi_global_v6_float/ with tiles.geojson. Report which version you used and why.
b. Download only the tiles that intersect the Malta grid bounding box (with a 200 m margin). Save to data/malta/canopy_meta/ and keep it out of git.
c. Record tile IDs and, if the metadata has them, the image acquisition dates per tile. Report the date range over Malta.

STEP 2. Canopy mask
a. Canopy = height of 3 m or more. Also compute 2 m and 5 m as sensitivity.
b. Work at the native 1 m resolution. Do not resample to 100 m before computing shares. Put the grid and the raster in the same CRS (reproject the vector, not the raster, if possible).

STEP 3. Street buffer
a. Streets from OpenStreetMap (reuse the walking network extract if it has highway tags; otherwise osmdata). Keep highway = primary, secondary, tertiary, residential, unclassified, living_street, pedestrian, trunk and their _link versions. Exclude service, track, footway, path, steps, cycleway, construction, proposed. Report the kept classes and total length.
b. Buffer 10 m each side of the centreline (sensitivity: 15 m). Dissolve, then intersect with the grid.
c. Main indicator: street_canopy_pct = canopy area inside the street buffer / street buffer area, per cell (%).
d. Cells with no street buffer: NA, not 0. They are then handled by the existing available weight rule. Report how many cells and how much population they hold.
e. Second alternative: cell_canopy_pct = canopy area / cell area (whole cell, no street restriction).
f. Airport and port constraint cells (459) are excluded as in the spec.

STEP 4. Quality checks (report all)
a. Distribution of street_canopy_pct: summary, share of cells at 0, number of distinct values, share at the most common value. Compare with perc_tree.
b. Spearman between street_canopy_pct and perc_tree; cross table "zero in Street Tree Layer" vs "zero in canopy".
c. Side by side maps (perc_tree vs street_canopy_pct) for three zooms: Valletta and Floriana, Sliema and Gżira, Ħamrun and Marsa. Add one panel per zoom with the canopy mask over a satellite basemap (visual check only). Use R/fig_style.R (theme_lancet(), save_fig()).

STEP 5. Rerun with the new indicator (citizen weights)
a. Normalise street_canopy_pct exactly as perc_tree is normalised now (same method, same direction: less canopy = higher priority).
b. Priority score with street_canopy_pct replacing perc_tree. Report Spearman with the current score, top quintile overlap, top 5 councils by share of cells in the top quintile (current vs _canopy), and the share of the score explained by street greenery in top quintile cells.
c. Step 3 (burden coincidence, Burden_coincidence_random_weights.Rmd logic, same tie rule): share of scored cells in the street greenery top class, count of cells in the top class of 3 or more criteria, observed vs shuffled ratio. Current vs _canopy in one table.
d. Repeat b and c for cell_canopy_pct and for the 2 m, 5 m and 15 m buffer variants, in one compact sensitivity table.

Follow MCDA_paper_results_spec.md. If anything here contradicts it, stop and ask before running.
Add Steps 7 and 8 to mcda/street_greenery_canopy_malta.Rmd. Do not overwrite any current file; new outputs keep the _canopy suffix. No hyphens in any text you write.

STEP 7. Fair comparison of the canopy indicator

7a. Option (b) as the main canopy variant. Eligible cells with no street buffer get street greenery criterion score = 0 ("not applicable": no street, no street tree need). This is NOT missing data: the 80% available weight rule is unchanged for every other criterion. Check that scored cells = 10,194, as in the current score.
Compare with the current score (Street Tree Layer): scored cells, Spearman, top quintile overlap, % of cells changing quintile, street greenery share of the score in top quintile cells, top 5 councils (current vs canopy, with %). Repeat the Step 5c table (street greenery top class %, % of cells in the top class of 3 or more criteria, shuffled %, ratio) under option (b).

7b. Populated cells. Keep the quintiles computed over all scored cells (as in the main map), then report among populated cells only (Total_Population > 0): Spearman, top quintile overlap, and the share of the population living in top quintile cells, current vs canopy.

7c. Variants compared directly with each other, not with the current score. All under option (b), all cells and populated cells:
- 10 m vs 15 m buffer (3 m height)
- 3 m vs 2 m height (10 m buffer)
- 3 m vs 5 m height (10 m buffer)
Report Spearman and top quintile overlap in one table.

STEP 8. Street half width in Malta (centreline to facade)

8a. Streets: the same kept OSM classes as Step 3. Buildings: OSM building footprints for the study area (osmdata or the existing extract). Report the number of buildings. If coverage looks incomplete in a visual check, say so and suggest Microsoft Global ML Building Footprints as an alternative (do not download it without asking).
8b. Transects: every 20 m along each kept street, a line perpendicular to the street, 30 m to each side of the centreline. Skip transects within 15 m of a street junction (they hit crossing streets or open space).
8c. Half width = distance from the centreline to the first building the transect meets, on each side separately. A side with no building within 30 m = NA (open side, not a street canyon). Full width = sum of both sides, only where both are measured.
8d. Report: number of transects and of measured sides; median, IQR, p75 and p90 of half width; the same by highway class and by Urban Atlas 2021 class of the cell (urban fabric classes separately); share of measured sides with half width up to 10 m and up to 15 m; median full width.
8e. Visual check: one figure with 3 zooms (a historic core such as Valletta or Birkirkara, Sliema, one newer residential area) showing transects and buildings over a satellite basemap (visual only). Use R/theme_lancet.R.

FINAL REPORT
Short summary with: the Step 7a, 7b and 7c tables, the Step 8d table, and one line saying whether the street half width supports a 10 m buffer (for example "median half width X m; Y% of measured sides within 10 m"). Flag anything odd. Do not commit.

OUTPUTS
- mcda/street_greenery_canopy_malta.Rmd and its HTML
- data/malta/street_greenery_canopy_cells.csv (cell ID, street_canopy_pct, cell_canopy_pct, variants, street buffer area)
- tables and figures with the _canopy suffix

FINAL REPORT
A short summary with: version and dates used, ties before and after, Spearman and overlap with the current score, Step 3 table, and anything odd. No hyphens in any text you write.
